sticker_location: The breaker panel door has a list of what each breaker feeds.

problems.title: An outlet stopped working
symptoms: Nothing works when I plug it in
The bathroom plug has no power

plan.diagnosis: Kitchen, bathroom, garage and outdoor outlets are protected by a GFCI outlet with TEST and RESET buttons. When it trips, it cuts that outlet and others down the line. Pressing RESET almost always brings them back.
tools: A lamp or phone charger to test
safety: Keep hands dry and stay away from water when pressing the buttons.
If an outlet is warm, scorched or smells burnt, leave it off and call an electrician.

details: The thing you plugged in may be what tripped it.
steps.check: Nothing is plugged into the dead outlet.

steps.instruction: Find the outlet with TEST and RESET buttons
details: Check kitchen, bathroom, garage and outside outlets.
steps.check: You've found it; it can be a few feet away from the dead one.

steps.instruction: Press RESET firmly until it clicks
details: If it won't stay in, the power may be off at the breaker.

steps.instruction: Plug in a lamp or phone charger to test
details: Test the dead outlet, not just the GFCI.

plan.diagnosis: If RESET didn't help, the breaker for that circuit has probably tripped. A tripped breaker sits in the middle, not fully on, and has to go all the way off before it goes back on.
safety: Never remove the panel's inner cover; only touch the breaker switches.
If a breaker trips again right away, stop and call an electrician.

details: It's often in the garage, basement or a hall closet.
steps.check: You can see the rows of breakers.

steps.instruction: Find the breaker that's in the middle
details: It may show a red or orange flag.
The label list on the door helps.
steps.check: You can see one breaker out of line with the rest.

steps.instruction: Push it fully OFF, then back ON
details: Push firmly; you'll feel it reset.
Stand to the side of the panel as you flip it.
steps.check: It clicks into the ON position and stays.

steps.instruction: Close the panel and test the outlet
details: If it trips again right away, leave it off and call an electrician.

rig_beats.caption: This one is out of line

problems.title: Breaker keeps tripping
symptoms: The power keeps going out in one room
It trips when I use the microwave and toaster

plan.diagnosis: A breaker that trips when several things run at once is overloaded: too many heaters, kettles or microwaves on one circuit. Spreading them out stops it. If it trips with nothing plugged in, that's a wiring fault for an electrician.
safety: If it trips with nothing plugged in, or you smell burning, call an electrician.

steps.instruction: Unplug the big heat makers on that circuit
details: Anything that heats draws the most power.
steps.check: Space heaters, kettles, toasters and hair dryers are unplugged.

steps.instruction: Reset the breaker: fully off, then on
Plug things back in one at a time
details: Move heaters and kettles to outlets on another circuit.
steps.check: You know which combination trips it.
